ADJOURNED MEETING

  CITY OF LA VERNE

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Tim Hepburn, Mayor  www.cityoflaverne.org
  (909) 596-8726 - Phone
Muir Davis, Mayor Pro Tem
  (909) 596-8740 - Fax
Robin Carder, Council Member
  City Hall Council Chamber
Rick Crosby, Council Member
  3660 D Street
Wendy M. Lau, Council Member  La Verne, CA 91750

  Monday, May 17, 2021 - 4:30 p.m.

  In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
  modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Clerk’s
  Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting. Regular Meetings are held on the 1st
  and 3rd Monday of every month.

  Tonight’s Council Meeting will again be closed to the public in compliance with Governor Newsom’s
  Executive Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-19 Virus. However, the City encourages public
  participation and as such wants to make residents aware of the following opportunities on how to
  participate:

  1)  View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org and click on the green
  “Council Meeting Live Stream” button.

  2)  Individuals can email their comments to the Assistant City Clerk at cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org up
  to noon on the day of the meeting. Those comments will be shared with City Council in advance
  of the City Council meeting and included as part of the permanent record. Please be advised
  that public comments submitted by emails or any other format to the City are public
  records that will be made available for public viewing.

  3)  Individual who wish to share their comments directly during the meeting may do so by emailing
  the Assistant City Clerk at cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org with their phone number and the item(s)
  they wish to speak on. Requests will be accepted before and throughout the meeting and staff
  will call you back at the appropriate time. Once items are considered by the City Council, no
  further public comment on that matter will be accepted. A time limit of 3-minutes is set for all
  public comments.

  4)  If  you  wish  to  participate  via  Zoom,  you  will  need  to  register  at
  https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_fdV2-LyuTbajWMzkxM992g before 3:00 p.m.
  on Monday, May 17, 2021, and please be aware that space is limited. You will have the ability to
  watch the meeting in real time and raise your hand to request to comment as appropriate on the
  current agenda item(s). Once it is your turn to speak, you will be brought into the meeting and
  have the ability to turn your video on when called upon.
  AGENDA, La Verne City Council Adjourned Meeting, Monday, May 17, 2021, Page 2

 1.  CALL TO ORDER

 2.  ROLL CALL:  Council Member Lau, Council Member Crosby, Council Member Carder,
  Mayor Pro Tem Davis and Mayor Hepburn.

 3.  The City Council will meet for a Study Session on the Preliminary Budget for Fiscal
  Year 2021-22 and on the Capitol Improvement Programs.

 4.  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS - This is the time set aside for anyone
  wishing to address the City Council on items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Under
  the provisions of the Brown Act, the legislative body is prohibited from talking or engaging in
  discussion on any item not appearing on the posted agenda. However, your concerns may be
  referred to staff or set for discussion at a later date. Please email your public comment to the
  Assistant City Clerk at cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org. Your public comment will be shared with the
  City Council and included as part of the permanent record. If you wish to speak, email your
  phone number and staff will call you back. There is a 3-minute time limit on public comments.

5.  ADJOURNMENT

  THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING of the La Verne City Council
  is scheduled for Monday, May 17, 2021, at 6:30 p.m.

  The La Verne City Council thanks the residents
  for taking all precautions to prevent the spread of the COVID-19 Virus.

 ADVISORY STAFF

 ____ Robert Russi, City Manager
 ____ Robert Kress, City Attorney
 ____ Lupe Gaeta Estrella, Assistant City Clerk
 ____ Mark Alvarado, Interim Finance Director
 ____Christy Lopez, Senior Management Analyst
 ____Shawn Igoe, Public Works Director

 Posting Statement: On May 11, 2021, a true and correct copy of this Agenda was posted
 on the bulletin board at La Verne City Hall, 3660 D Street, La Verne, and on the City’s
 website at cityoflaverne.org.

MINUTES OF AN ADJOURNED  MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE
  Monday, May 17, 2021

1.  In order to minimize the spread of the COVID- 19 Virus, Governor Newsom issued an Executive Order that
  temporarily suspends requirements of the Brown Act. The Council Chambers was closed to the public, La Verne
  City Council Members attended this meeting telephonically, and meeting was live streamed on the City' s website.
2.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 4:31 p. m.

3.  Council Members present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Muir Davis
  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel  present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  Assistant to the City Manager JR Ranells
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Interim Finance Director Mark Alvarado
  Senior Management Analyst Christy Lopez
  Public Works Director Shawn Igoe

4.  Council Study Session on the  The City Council met in a Study Session on the Preliminary Budget for Fiscal
  Preliminary Budget for Fiscal  Year 2021- 22 and on the Capital Improvement Programs.
  Year 2021- 22 and on the
  Capital Improvement Programs.
  Public Works Director Igoe reported on the Capitol Improvement Programs
  with  a slide  presentation.

  One communication was received via the webinar.

  City Manager Russi reported on the 2021- 22 preliminary budget with a slide
  presentation.

  After discussion on the budget, Mayor Hepburn stated that he has put together
  a plan to start the rebuilding process for the Fire Department and asked for
  Council  support.  He proposed using the City reserves, and it would cost the
  1. 2 million to 1. 5 million per year.

  The City Council discussed the pros and cons of Mayor Hepburn' s proposal.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  Eight ( 8) phone communications received.

  To hear what was said during public comment, please visit the City's website
  to view the archived Council meeting.

  Nine  public comments  received  via email are attached.
   City Council Minutes, Adjourned Meeting, Monday, May 17, 2021,  Page 2

  After City Council further discussed Mayor Hepburn' s proposal, a roll call vote
  was taken. Support for the proposed fire plan failed by a vote of 1- 4( Davis,

  Carder, Crosby  and  Lau voted  No.  Council Members who voted No, stated that
  fire services and public safety are crucial, but taking funds from the City' s
  reserves for a recurring expense is not a financially sustainable solution.

  It was the consensus of the majority of the City Council to direct staff to do a
  contract for a Standards of Coverage Report on how best to address services
  provided by the La Verne Fire Department.

  They directed staff to move forward with budget preparation for a further study
  session  at  June 7, 2021,  Council meeting.

  Mayor Hepburn stated he was disappointed with Council' s lack of support.

5.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other  place  on  the agenda.  Mayor Hepburn called for
  public comment and waited for staff to check for any public comment via
  telephone communication.

  Mayor Hepburn  called for public comment.

  There was none.

6.  Adjournment at 6: 26 p. m.

  Respectfully submitted,

  Lupe Gaeta Estrella,  CMC
  Assistant  City Clerk

Greetings Mr. Mayor and City Council

I am amazed and I' m sure most citizens are as well, that we have gone from a budget crunch, loss of tax
revenue due to the pandemic and recent fire department concerns to a new, possible revelation that we will
have funding to dramatically change our fire department.

To imagine that we will be back with positive growth in the fire department, hiring more firefighters, opening
a closed fire station, and upgrading equipment is music to our ears!

Now, the big question: "  Where  is the money coming from?" I can only assume we owe a debt of gratitude  to
our  city manager  and  staff for the fiscal responsibility they have provided. Along with that, we are so
fortunate to have thriving restaurants, like Chases, that are busy and producing great sales tax revenue.

Many of us remember that we had to borrow money to fund the liability regarding public employee' s
pensions.  In a few years  we  will  be facing that again.  Along with that, how about other services that have
been reduced or cut back?

While it is good news that we might not have to take a vote about our fire department going county, we are
left to wonder if decisions will be made that will come back to haunt us later on.

Being our elected representatives, we look forward to the decisions and transparency you present as you vote

Greetings
Please share the comments below with City Council members,
the City Manager, and attendees at the Budget Study Session later today.
We are long time residents of La Verne and are aware of a recent plan
prepared by Mayor Hepburn regarding enlarging the Fire Dept.
We have been advised that Mr. Hepburn' s plan has not been reviewed
by the City manager or City Council members. In addition, we have been
advised the plan does not provide a strategy to pay for proposed
increased Fire Dept.  staff.  Finally, we recall the costly damage to the City resulting
from Mr. Hepburn' s direct involvement with the La Verne Fire Dept. Union.
Accordingly, we strongly recommend the following precautions concerning
Mr. Hepburn' s plan:
1. The plan should be thoroughly reviewed by the City Manager and Council Members
  prior to consideration of implementation.
2. The plan should be fully endorsed by the City Manager and Council Members prior
  to adoption.
3. Because the City may be close to hiring a new Fire Chief, it would be prudent to
  defer consideration of the Hepburn plan until the new Fire Chief has reviewed, and potentially
  revised the plan.
4. Most importantly, the Hepburn plan should not be adopted until a strategy to pay for the
  increased Fire Dept. staff has been established and approved by the City Manager and City Council.
Thank you

Re: Fire Department Funding

Dear Mayor and La Verne City Councilmembers,

I have lived in La Verne for 18 years and one of the outstanding things about the city is its sense of
  and  its public safety infrastructure.  One of the most important concerns of most
community
citizens  and  businesses  in any community is public safety.  From an economic development

standpoint, public safety is a major consideration when businesses look to locate or expand in a city.

This letter is to express support for the mayor' s proposal to reopen Fire Station No. 3, add one
additional ambulance and increase staffing levels with the goal of ineeting industry- standard
recommended number of fire personnel needed to address building fires. Given the fire season we
had in 2020, it is key that La Verne is prepared.  With this support comes additional comments for
you to consider.

First and foremost,  public  safety is of the utmost importance
  to me.  As a resident I want to see fully
functional La Verne police and fire departments with adequate staffing and equipment to provide
the highest level  of  safety for the community.
  In addition, I want a plan in place for both fire and
police  that is sustainable  over  the long term.  My ideal is to have local police and fire departments
and I do support a budget that addresses that but let me make it clear, the community' s public
safety is the priority.

I sit on the LV Sales Tax Oversight Review Committee and the LV sales tax measure was supported
by many because of the fact that a portion of the additional revenues would be used to support
public  safety.  I support the allocation of funds that results in a fully functional and sustainable
public safety ( fire and  police)  infrastructure ( staff, equipment, etc.).  I also say this with the opinion
that maintaining our city' s infrastructure ( streets, sidewalks, parks and technology) also be
adequately addressed. For your information, the lV Oversight Review Committee will be meeting on
lune 1 to discuss the current city budget and address any recommendations.

Thank you for your  consideration of  my comments. The opinions  expressed  are my own.

 Marlene  Carney

Good afternoon Council Members, Mr. Russi

Any proposal for such changes to be made without the input from our New Fire
Chief could be unnecessarily counterproductive and premature.

This appears  to be a wish list of current  departmental  employees  instead  of an
analysis of operational data to support such change to the operational model.

Best business  practices  require that to change the Fire Department
organizationally,  we need the input of the person who will be responsible to the
City Manager and Council in coming years, and that will be the New Fire Chief. To
proceed with this type of change before the New Fire Chief has had the
operational opportunity to fully analyze the organizational  needs is imprudent.
The New Fire Chief will bring his own operational experiences from a different but
similar background and using those work life experiences along with an analysis of
the operational data is more likely to result in a better operational model
proposal.  Let' s give him the time to fully digest and analyze the challenges before
him instead of making those decisions that may unnecessarily limit his and our
success.

Organizational structure is not something that should be decided with one or two
Council Members meeting with current Fire Department personnel, especially
when one of them, the Interim Fire Chief has already submitted his intention to
resign.  Changes such as recommended in this proposal need much more analysis
and  as to being fiscally prudent from an overall perspective.

would deplete our reserves in approximately 6 years.

We need to address reinstating the Firefighters Paramedic Premium Pay before

I appreciate  that you will each give this matter independent  and thoughtful
